Subject: Inquiry: VPC pricing model — subscription vs metered

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this initial request. We're evaluating Redwood for a private VPC deployment and need a clear comparison between: 1) an annual subscription / platform fee model (fixed commitment), and 2) a metered/consumption approach (variable, usage-based). Key asks from procurement:

- High-level cost comparison (3-year TCO) for a realistic workload of ~200 concurrent sessions, peak 1.2M tokens/day.
- How platform fee, per-node licensing, and support tiers interact with discounts/credits.
- Migration/exit protections (exit cap, transferability of on-prem license).
- Evidence for SOC 2 / audit artifacts for procurement review.

I've attached our RFP with workload assumptions. Can your team send a short two-option breakdown and an initial ballpark quote so procurement can prioritize?

Attachment: CloudCorp_RFP.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,

Alex — thanks for the RFP. Ben and I reviewed it with Marcus and sketched two pragmatic options that map to how customers typically buy Private (VPC / on-prem). Attached is a spreadsheet with line items; below is the short summary so procurement can move quickly.

Attachment: Redwood_Initial_Pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Option A — Subscription-first (recommended for predictable spend)\- Annual platform subscription: covers control plane, telemetry, and coordinated rollouts. Example: $420,000/year for your stated footprint (includes platform licensing + software updates).\- Node license: $6,800 per GPU-equipped node/month (or a workshop to size exact node counts).\- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 4hr P1), Premium (24/7, 1hr P1)\- Discounts: 15% off platform fee for 12-month commit; 22% for 24-month commit.\- Benefits: predictable budgeting, included upgrade automation, and higher SLA.\\n
Option B — Lower platform fee + consumption overlay (recommended if you expect large volatility)\- Platform subscription reduced to $180,000/year.\- Consumption fee: metered inference units (billing per 1k tokens-equivalent delivered by the private runtime) — estimated $0.35/1k tokens at your scale, with volume bands.\- Support: Premium recommended for bursty workloads.\- Discounts: volume tiers reduce per-1k price after threshold; platform fee discount only on multi-year commit.\- Benefits: lower baseline, elastic cost if usage is variable, slightly higher operational variance.

Other points
- Migration/Exit: we can provide an exit cap in the SOW that limits total termination liability to 6 months of platform fee or a negotiated cap.\- On-prem license transferability: we allow SSO/key transfer with a standard transfer SLA; there are one-time re-certification fees if hardware topology changes materially.\- SOC 2: we'll provide the SOC 2 Type II report and an evidence package under an NDA.

Next steps I recommend: 1) confirm expected average daily tokens or attach a sample production trace; 2) indicate preferred commit term for discounting; 3) let us know if you need an enterprise legal term sheet for procurement.

We can jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Alex — thanks, read the procurement doc. Quick summary of what we can commit to today and what requires legal review: 

Commercial concessions (subject to signature)
- Platform fee: we can extend a 20% discount on the annual platform subscription for a 24-month committed term (final discount anchored to deal value / node count).
- One-time onboarding credit: $60,000 of professional services credits to cover initial deployment validation and runbook authoring.
- Exit cap: we are prepared to accept a termination cap equal to 6 months of the then-current platform fee (this is our standard outside of special exceptions). For higher limits we can consider an escrow arrangement — legal would need to draft.

Support and SLA
- Premium support (recommended): 24/7 coverage, 1-hour P1 response, service credits in SOW: 10% credit for each 1 hour of P1 downtime, up to 100% of monthly platform fee for prolonged outages. Precise SLA language to be circulated by Legal.

Security and networking
- Metered variant: inference can run fully inside your VPC. The control plane needs limited outbound connectivity for telemetry and licensing (mutually agreed endpoints; optional private peering). We will provide the SOC 2 Type II and sample audit artifacts after NDA.

Counter-proposal on discount
- We cannot accept a 30% platform fee reduction at this stage. Our counter is 20% + the $60k onboarding credit for a 24-month commitment. If we agree to the 20% now, Ben can extend a one-time additional 5% coupon on node-license rates for the first 12 months (conditional on signature within 30 days).

Next actions
1) I will ask Legal to prepare a term sheet that includes the exit cap and SLA bullets.
2) Ben will prepare a final HubSpot quote reflecting the 20% platform discount and PS credit.
3) Please send a sample production token trace or confirm expected monthly tokens for the billing model.

Ben/Marcus — Ben, please prepare the quote + updated line items. Marcus, please coordinate the SOC 2 evidence package so we can share under NDA.

Thanks,
Kim
